author: Gould, 1841
habitat: 해안 갯벌, 하구, 내륙 물가의 트인 땅
summary: 4~5월과 9~10월쯤 우리나라를 지나가는 희귀한 나그네새로, 해안 갯벌과 하구, 내륙 물가의 트인 곳에 산다. 갑각류, 복족류, 모족류 등을 주로 먹는다. 국내에서는 개성, 연안, 용암포 등지에서 관찰되었다. 시베리아와 몽골 등 동아시아에서 번식하고 필리핀, 오스트레일리아 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Little Curlew (Numenius minutus), adult as seen in Korea on spring passage (April–May; plumage similar all year): crown blackish-brown with a narrow buff central stripe; broad pale buff supercilium; pale lores and a thin dark brown stripe behind the eye; cheeks, neck sides and hindneck pale buff with fine dark streaks; chin and throat pale buff; upperparts blackish-brown with buff notches and fringes; breast buff finely streaked dark, belly whitish-buff with little marking; rump and tail brown, the tail barred blackish-brown; undertail coverts pale buff barred brown. Short, slightly decurved dark bill with a pinkish base to the lower mandible; dark eye; legs bluish-grey.
art.pose: walking on open ground near water, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal mudflat and open ground by an estuary during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing on short grass: blackish-brown crown with a buff central stripe, broad pale buff supercilium, thin dark eye-stripe, pale buff neck finely streaked, blackish-brown back with buff fringes, short gently decurved bill, bluish-grey legs
adult in flight seen from above: uniform brown upperwing and back with no white on the rump, brown tail barred blackish-brown, short gently decurved bill
art.build: Small curlew, about 33cm long, about the size of a feral pigeon and much smaller than Whimbrel; slim and long-legged, with a small rounded head and a gentle, plover-like expression. Bill short for a curlew — only a little longer than the head — fairly thin, nearly straight for most of its length and gently decurved towards the tip. Legs medium-long, bluish-grey. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight uniform brown upperparts with no white on the rump or back, and buffish, barred underwings.
avoid: Do not paint a long, strongly curved bill — that is Whimbrel or Eurasian Curlew; this bill is short and only gently decurved.
Do not paint a white rump or a white wedge up the back (Whimbrel).
Do not paint a dark loral stripe joining the eye to the bill; the lores are pale.
Do not paint golden-spangled upperparts (Pacific Golden Plover).
